title: Relief from Cart Path for a Left-Handed Stance
question: A right-handed player's ball comes to rest beside a tree, blocking any reasonable right-handed stroke. The player could reasonably play the ball left-handed. In taking a left-handed stance, their feet are on an artificially surfaced cart path. Is the player entitled to free relief from the cart path?

choices.text: Yes, provided the left-handed stroke is reasonable in the circumstances.
No, free relief is not allowed because the player is right-handed.
No, free relief cannot be taken for a stance used only to seek relief.
Yes, but only if their clubs are designed for left-handed play.

explanation: Under Rule 16.1, a player is entitled to free relief from an immovable obstruction, such as a cart path, if it interferes with the player’s area of intended stance or swing. If playing left-handed is a reasonable stroke in the circumstances, interference for a left-handed stroke entitles the player to relief, even if the player is usually right-handed. After taking relief for the left-handed stance, the player is not required to play the next stroke left-handed if a right-handed stroke is possible from the new lie.
